findings.description: Priority 1 recommendation "Give every custom control an accessible name and the correct role and state…" is generic, lacks a selector or page reference, and can be copy‑pasted into any audit.
Priority 2 recommendation "Raise the contrast ratio of the flagged text…" is generic, no specific element or count, making it a copy‑pasteable template.
Priority 3 recommendation "Expose the structure a sighted user sees…" lacks any data anchor and can be applied to any site.
Priority 4 recommendation "Review the flagged instances against the relevant standard…" is generic, no selector or page URL.
Priority 5 recommendation "Add descriptive alt text to the informative images that lack it…" does not reference specific images or counts.
Priority 6 recommendation "Order headings without skipping levels…" is generic, no heading selector or page context.
Priority 7 recommendation "Wrap the primary content of each page in a single `<main>` landmark…" lacks a specific page reference.
Priority 8 recommendation "Replace the obvious landmark containers (header, nav, main, footer, aside) with their semantic elements…" is generic and not tied to any selector or count.
Priority 9 recommendation "Add the missing response headers at the server or CDN edge…" does not name specific headers or configuration details.
Priority 10 recommendation "Add the missing required and recommended Schema.org properties to the flagged entity types…" lacks a selector, page URL, or count.
Priority 11 recommendation "Publish the missing discovery file at the site root…" is generic and not tied to any specific path or vendor.
Priority 12 recommendation "Publish the missing discovery file at the site root…" repeats the same generic recommendation as Priority 11.

The report contains internal comment lines in the YAML front matter (e.g., "# The single cog that manages this pipeline artefact…") and other explanatory comments that are not intended for client delivery, indicating leaked AI generation artifacts.
